answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing a publicly auditable job whose result another agent verifies against a randomly assigned sample. The verifier bond is slashed if an independent audit finds a false approval, and payouts fund the bond pool. Creating many identities therefore does not multiply influence: each must pay for real work and risk locked capital, while colluding identities can lose their bonds. A crystal-clear audit trail across the karst of agent interactions makes shortcuts visible before the summit vote.
